clue.text: Some fish move off to bank caught by line

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it in reserve, so the word for 'move off' keeps the letter for 'caught' inside it

parts.note: shoo is the order telling someone to move off
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Some fish swim away from the riverbank only to be hooked on an angler's line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some fish' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: a group of fish. 'by' just puts L next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is the collective noun for a large group of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Harvester might be located here — the fourteenth food and drink outlet?

parts.note: a bar is a place serving drinks and snacks
N is the fourteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Harvester is a British chain of pub restaurants, so the clue seems to ask where the fourteenth branch might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface treats Harvester as a restaurant brand; in the definition it is a farm machine, a combine harvester, stored in a farm building. A barn dance also fits the puzzle's dance theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is the farm building where machinery such as a combine harvester is kept.

clue.text: Female model let several houses when erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something stands it upright, so the letters read from bottom to top
the run of words 'model let several' houses, or holds, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A woman lets out several houses she has had built as a model development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' marks the hidden letters EL LET SE across 'model let several'; 'when erected' then turns ELLETSE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Estelle is a woman's given name, so a girl's name stands for a female.

clue.text: Amount of power church gets in two areas is necessary in Africa

parts.note: kW, the kilowatt, is a unit measuring power

indicators.note: the church abbreviation gets in between the two area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, taken twice

explanation.surface: A statement that an African project needs electricity, a church and two land areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the necessary' is slang for money, so 'necessary in Africa' is an African currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The kwacha is the currency of Zambia and Malawi, and money is colloquially called the necessary.

clue.text: Bird needing hand to secure belt before journey

indicators.note: the word for hand holds the word for belt firmly inside it

parts.note: fin is slang for a hand
to belt or lam someone is to hit them hard
a go is a turn or trip, here a journey

explanation.surface: A bird needs someone's help to fasten its seat belt before setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is a verb meaning hit, not a strap. 'before' just orders the pieces. The flamingo is also a dance, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: Royal tea regulations not universal

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: 'not universal' says the letter for universal is left out

parts.note: rules are regulations
U is the British film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family finds that the rules about tea do not apply to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles is the name of a royal, the heir and now King of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Gander seen up river in Cornish port

indicators.note: the reversed river sits in the port name

parts.note: Looe is a fishing port in Cornwall, south-west England

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the Esk is a river name used in several parts of Britain

explanation.surface: A goose is spotted heading upstream into a harbour in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like a male goose, but here it is British slang for a look. 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is informal British for having a glance, the same as a quick peek.

clue.text: Shake rapidly, as wife replaces husband in negotiation

indicators.note: the wife letter takes the place of the husband letter

parts.note: to haggle is to bargain, a negotiation over price

explanation.surface: A wife takes over from her husband in tense talks, shaking rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To waggle is to move something quickly to and fro, a quick jiggling motion.

clue.text: Gossips head outpouring from chemical plant?

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, so one who gossips gases
a cape is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Gossips spread the word about a leak at a chemical works.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak of fumes from a factory site is an escape of gas into the air.

clue.text: Geordie inhabits Teesside location briefly — it's an alien territory

indicators.note: the Geordie lives inside the shortened name of the Teesside town

parts.note: Boro is the short name for Middlesbrough, a town on the River Tees
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A Newcastle man settles in Middlesbrough, a place that feels foreign to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies and Middlesbrough people are North East rivals, which is why Teesside would feel alien to one. 'it's an' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia, a foreign land as seen from Britain.

clue.text: Pardon former copper using mobile in butcher's

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the mobile letter goes in the word for look

parts.note: butcher's hook is Cockney rhyming slang for look, so a butcher's means a look, to see
M is an abbreviation for mobile

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman uses his phone in a butcher's shop and has to apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. 'Have a butcher's' is London rhyming slang for have a look. 'using' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying pardon is a polite request to be excused, an apology for interrupting.

clue.text: After competition's opening, enter jam

indicators.note: the word for enter is placed after the opening letter
the opening of the word competition is its first letter

parts.note: to log is to enter data in a record

explanation.surface: Once a contest opens, the entrants squeeze in and cause a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog is to block up, just as a jam blocks a passage.

clue.text: Vocal support for magician who performs in church hall?

parts.note: Go! is a shouted cheer of encouragement
a speller here is one who casts spells

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up for a stage conjuror playing a church hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go, speller!' is a cheer for a magician. The question mark marks the loose definition: a gospel hall is a church hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller reads the Gospel at a service or preaches it, as at a gospel hall.

clue.text: Seasoning it repeatedly entertains character starting lunch

indicators.note: the doubled letters host the lunch letter between them
the word for it appears twice

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it

indicators.note: the character starting lunch is its first letter

explanation.surface: A seasoning keeps turning up, laid on for the start of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy sauce or relish used to flavour food. It is also a dance, part of the theme.

clue.text: Yellowish-brown hospital department

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a type of hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital department decorated in a dull beige colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand as a colour is a pale yellowish brown, the shade of a beach.

clue.text: Army medics do tea, breaking outside container and side dish

parts.note: M*A*S*H, the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital, was a US army medical unit

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit outside the container word
breaking the words do and tea leaves their letters scrambled

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Army doctors are making tea when someone breaks a container outside.
explanation.walkthrough: M*A*S*H was the field hospital of the US film and TV series. 'breaking' is the anagram signal and 'outside' wraps the result round the container. The mashed potato is also a dance, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato is a common accompaniment served beside the main part of a meal.

clue.text: Idle lying with rejection of rules constant? Armstrong did this

parts.note: to moon about is to idle aimlessly

indicators.note: rejecting the word for rules turns it back to front

parts.note: the law is a body of rules
k is a standard symbol for a constant in science

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about rejecting the rules, though Armstrong was a man of firm principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Neil Armstrong walking on the Moon; the moonwalk is also a dance step, part of the theme. 'lying' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong was the first astronaut to step on the lunar surface in 1969.

clue.text: See 16
Forest-dweller perhaps acquires property in US city

parts.note: an oak is one example of a tree living in a forest
land is property, as in owning land

explanation.surface: A woodland creature buys a plot of land in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest-dweller' suggests an animal, but it is a tree; 'perhaps' marks an example. 'acquires' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakland is a city in California, across the bay from San Francisco.

clue.text: Not for the first time, go up on branch with Charlie

definitions.text: Not for the first time, go up

parts.note: re means on or concerning
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a limb is a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a tree again, up on a branch beside a friend called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend once more is to scale something again, a repeat ascent.

clue.text: Support Lech Walesa?

definitions.meaning: a post or staff that holds something up
Lech Walesa, Solidarity leader and president of Poland, is an example of a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A call to back the Polish trade union leader Lech Walesa.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is a supporting post, and a Pole is a person from Poland.

clue.text: Split pedal audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word for pedal is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: the brake is a pedal in a car

explanation.surface: A bicycle pedal splits and makes a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To split something is to fracture it into pieces.

clue.text: Canadian singer drinks drop of Buck's Fizz?

indicators.note: the singer's name takes in a letter as if drinking it

parts.note: Michael Bublé is a Canadian crooner

indicators.note: a drop of a word is a tiny bit of it, its first letter

explanation.surface: A Canadian crooner sips a Buck's Fizz, champagne mixed with orange juice.
explanation.walkthrough: Fizz is the effervescence of bubbles in a drink; the question mark flags that one bubble stands for fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizz consists of gas pockets rising in a drink, each one a little sphere of air.

clue.text: Little space writer's given for award

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
the writer's means the setter's, so my

explanation.surface: A writer is given a little space to compensate for missing out on an award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the annual US television prize, presented as a statuette.

clue.text: Old Lib Dem leader keeps attending congress

indicators.note: the nickname keeps the word for attending inside it

parts.note: Sir Menzies (Ming) Campbell led the UK Liberal Democrats from 2006 to 2007
at means attending, as at a party

explanation.surface: A former British party leader is still going to political conferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' suggests a political gathering, but here it means sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress in its old sense is sexual intercourse, the union of a couple.

clue.text: Brand new ball relocated on centre-spot?

parts.note: a centre-spot or dot is a small circle, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the letters of new ball are moved into a different order

explanation.surface: A new football is moved to the centre spot for kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. The centre-spot reads as a football pitch marking, but here it is the shape O.
explanation.definitionFit: An own-label product carries the retailer's own brand rather than a maker's name.

clue.text: Sports broadcaster showing skill describing crowd

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the skill word goes round the crowd word

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
a lot is a group of people, a crowd

explanation.surface: A sports commentator shows skill describing the crowd at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: John Arlott was a famous BBC cricket commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: John Arlott was a celebrated radio voice of cricket, a commentator for the BBC.

clue.text: Extreme band leader

definitions.meaning: furthest or final, at the very end
James ... was a German big band leader

explanation.surface: An outrageous leader of a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Last means final or furthest, and James Last led a popular easy-listening orchestra.

clue.text: Fellow trainee takes type of test associated with climbers, say

parts.note: L is for learner, a trainee driver
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A fellow trainee sits a test associated with mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers, but means climbing plants, so 'say' marks an example of flowers. 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means relating to flowers, and climbing plants such as roses are often flowering ones.

clue.text: Cycle event from French house includes first stage to Dijon

indicators.note: the French word takes the first letter of Dijon inside it

parts.note: maison is French for house

indicators.note: the first stage of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cycle race stage from a French house to Dijon, like a Tour de France leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Madison is a track cycling relay race, and also a line dance, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madison is a track cycling relay race for pairs, named after Madison Square Garden.
